Subject: Commit definitions refresh + coaching materials

Team —

As discussed on last week's ops sync, finance wants clearer alignment on what we mark as Commit vs Best Case vs Pipeline. I took a pass and attached a short definitions doc plus a proposed one-page checklist we can use in 1:1s and manager calibration. High level:

- Commit: signed PO, contract countersigned, or explicit legal/finance approval tied to a start date. Forecast to month of first invoice.
- Best Case: verbal agreement + active procurement but missing signatures or final budget code.
- Pipeline: qualified opportunity with clear use case and champion but >60 days to close or unclear budget owner.

Please review the attached commit-definitions-v2.pdf and the slide deck. I want us to run two 45-minute coaching sessions next week (M/T) for AE+AMs to walk through examples and calibration exercises. Can you: 

1) Laura — incorporate any legal/procurement nuance we've seen in EMEA or large enterprise renewals.
2) Marissa — pull 3 Live deals (one renewal, one expansion, one trial) that we can use as practice cases, ideally including BrightWave.
3) Karthik — confirm the Ops calendar invites and the HubSpot update steps so managers can update Commitment status cleanly.

Thanks — I want the sales leaders to be able to justify changes to finance with clear evidence during the next forecast review.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — quick pass attached with two recommended clarifications: one for government procurement (PO timing vs signature) and one for channel-influenced deals where partner SOWs sometimes lag. I added an appendix with sample evidence items we can ask for when labeling a deal Commit (signed SOW, PO number + planned start, billing contact confirmation).

My edits are small, but I do recommend we 1) call out "billing contact confirmation" as required evidence for renewals and 2) add a fallback category for "Pending Legal" with a defined 14-day escalation path so finance isn't surprised.

I'll also update the slide deck to include a 10-minute calibration quiz.
